The bathrooms exhaust through this unit instead of separate fans (Maxwell, 11/17/2026). The code allows it because the ERV sends that air outdoors; it has to run continuously at 20 CFM or more per bathroom. Three baths plus whole house ventilation (about 75 CFM for this size and bedroom count) is near the top of a 100 CFM unit, so Andy should confirm the size. The range hood cannot connect here, it has its own duct outdoors.

info.model: 14 x 8 in, in the floor truss space
notes: New, in addition to Andy's main return. Each bedroom has a low grille near the floor (Maxwell, 11/17/2026) with a wall stack up the stud bay into the trusses. The builder plans open web floor trusses, so bedrooms 2 and 3 get a ducted return in the truss space instead of relying only on transfer grilles. It runs north to south in one truss bay at x 7.5 ft, parallel to the trusses, so it never crosses a supply run: every supply drop in the trusses leaves the trunk south side further east, and the bedroom 3 supply stops short of this bay. Trusses are 11-7/8 in deep with about 8-7/8 in clear between the chords, so the duct is 8 in tall. Size, truss direction and bay are ASSUMED until Andy or the HVAC installer sizes them.
